requirement: A user may have at most one rating per dish; a duplicate rating by the same user for the same dish is prevented.
label: INFERRED
evidence: ensure_indexes() creates a unique compound index on ratings: mongo.db.ratings.create_index([("dish_id", 1), ("user_id", 1)], unique=True). In POST /ratings, the inserted document includes both dish_id and user_id, and mongo.db.ratings.insert_one(doc) is wrapped in except PyMongoError: return error_response("Bad request", 400), so a second rating by the same user for the same dish is rejected.
reasoning: The code clearly contains behavior addressing the requirement: a database-level unique constraint on (dish_id, user_id) enforces at most one rating per user per dish. A duplicate POST for the same authenticated user and dish would violate that index and be prevented, causing the request to fail. Per the decision guide, equivalent enforcement via a unique index fully satisfies the requirement, so this is INFERRED.
